content: A superficial vein refers to a vein located near the surface of the body. This term is used to distinguish these veins from deep veins, which are situated further beneath the surface. Unlike deep veins, superficial veins are not accompanied by an artery running alongside them. Deep veins, on the other hand, are typically paired with an artery of the same name. Superficial veins play a physiological role in thermoregulation. When the body becomes overheated, blood is redirected from the deep veins to the superficial veins to facilitate heat dissipation to the external environment. These veins are often visible beneath the skin, and those located below the level of the heart tend to protrude or bulge outward. A simple way to observe this phenomenon is by raising your hand above your heart, which causes the blood in the superficial veins to drain, or lowering it below your heart, which causes the veins to fill with blood. Superficial veins become more prominent under certain conditions, such as during heavy weightlifting or after consistent strength training. Despite their visibility, superficial veins are less critical physiologically compared to deep veins, as they carry a smaller volume of blood. In some cases, superficial veins are surgically removed in a procedure called vein stripping, which is commonly performed to treat varicose veins. Examples of Named Superficial Veins: External Jugular Vein Superficial Veins of the Upper Limb: Cephalic Vein Median Cubital Vein: This vein is frequently used for venipuncture (blood drawing).
